title: A Periodical's review ticket doesn't run the Surveys
description:
## As asked

**Repository:** JKershaw/LinearViewer (Harbour).

**What this is for.** Every fresh task starts with two Surveys, one on the task and one on the place. For tasks that change code they have earned their keep. John: "whilst it's tempted to do a single review, we did find benefits from two." A Periodical's own review ticket changes no code, yet runs both today. John: "Happy to skip for periodicals though."

**What we want.** A Periodical's review ticket goes to its work without the Surveys. Every other task keeps both.

**Done when** a minted Periodical's review ticket runs without the Surveys, and other tasks still get both.

**Every change names what it retires. Questions:** settle engineering questions yourself; only John's calls (product, money, authority, what to retire) go to him as rulings.

*End of what was asked. Steps write below this line; nothing above it changes.*

## Size of the move

**Size:** just the task
**Why:** A gate-marked Periodical review ticket starts at scoping while every other fresh ticket keeps both Surveys; no Survey finding binds, since the honest reason text and the doc exceptions are part of the asked change itself.
**Cuts:** none
**Decided by:** the standing policy

## Implementation Plan

fits one session
plan-review due: no

Implemented as approved in [PR #2391](<https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2391>), merged as `008d38bb088ca824f433940a227bffc27f3a60a1` and deployed: `isPeriodicalReview` in `lib/periodicals.js`, a per-ticket `lookFirstSteps` in `lib/recommendation-look-first.js` with the `why` built from it, tests, and one clause in each doc that described the old rule. A gate-marked Periodical review starts at scoping with no Surveys; every other ticket keeps both. The only deviation: the planned `## Waiting` entry was not added, because `docs/areas/llm-and-prompts.md` is at its byte cap; ruling `lin4398-area-note-cap` is open for John. Review's one fix (`docs/plans/survey.md:96`) landed as `821ef78a0`. The plan, research and Survey findings are preserved in the task snapshots and the comment trail.

comments.body:
## Survey open-0: LIN-4398 @ a36ad6195

**Where the change goes.** Both Surveys are sent from one place: the look-first route (`lib/recommendation-look-first.js`, `LOOK_FIRST_STEPS = ['survey-task','survey-place','scoping']`). It is reached only through `codeRouteOf` in `lib/openrouter.js:2115`, and both the task page and recommend-and-dispatch use that path, as does the scoped autopilot kickoff a Stage-1 Periodical fires. The minted ticket is sealed when it's created (POST /issues seals any non-empty description), and the gate marker becomes the first line inside its `## As asked` block. So it passes every `lookFirstOff` check, which is why it gets both Surveys today. The signal for "this is a Periodical's review ticket" already exists: `extractPeriodicalGateId(description)` in `lib/periodicals.js`, which the Done gate also uses. No new field or label is needed. The fix is small. These are the parts that could still go wrong:

1. **What about scoping?** The ask says "without the Surveys", and scoping is the third step in the same sequence. My reading is that scoping stays: the ask names only the Surveys, and scoping's prompt already reads Survey comments only "where they exist". The person doing the work should state this choice on the ticket so nobody has to guess it.
2. **The `why` text would be wrong.** `lookFirstStep` builds its reason from `LOOK_FIRST_STEPS.slice(0, index)`. If the Surveys are filtered out but that slice stays the same, scoping's reason says "survey-task and survey-place have been attempted", which isn't true. Build the step list for each ticket and work out the reason from that list.
3. **The premise is a little off.** The ticket says a review ticket "changes no code". In fact a Stage-2 run lands a docs-only PR with the report plus area-note edits, and goes through review and close-out (`lib/periodicals.js` header, LIN-4390/LIN-4379). That's no argument against John's ruling, which was "happy to skip for periodicals". But the change should name the right reason and the right retirement. It retires the two Survey runs on gate-marked tickets, and with them survey-place's reading of the area-note edits those tickets land.
4. **The marker is written by an agent.** The Stage-1 agent pastes the marker in itself. If a run leaves it out, the ticket still gets Surveys, and it also escapes the Done gate. That's the same failure that exists today, and this change shouldn't try to fix it. A hand-pasted marker on an ordinary ticket would also skip the Surveys. That's acceptable, since the Done gate already trusts the marker.
5. **Prose describing the old rule.** These places say "a fresh ticket gets both Surveys" and need a one-clause exception: `lib/proxy-instructions.js:920`, the look-first module docblock, and `docs/plans/survey.md`. The manual `kind: survey-task` override should keep working on Periodical tickets.

**What I'd do first.** Add two cases to `tests/unit/lin-4370-look-first-route.test.js`. The first is a sealed description whose first line inside the block is `buildPeriodicalGateMarker('Documentation Review')`: assert that the step is `scoping` and that the reason doesn't mention Surveys. The second is the same ticket without the marker: assert that the step is still `survey-task`. After that, make `LOOK_FIRST_STEPS` a per-ticket list inside `lookFirstStep`. "Done when" needs a real minted ticket to prove it, so check the run list of the first Periodical that runs after merge.

## Survey global: LIN-4398 @ a36ad6195

**Where it lands.** `lib/recommendation-look-first.js`, the third code route in `lib/openrouter.js` `codeRouteOf`. Both seams and the Mint + Autopilot path go through it. The module is young (LIN-4370) and well kept: LIN-4392 moved the live wait out, and the leftovers PRs keep the comments accurate. It is improving, though its docblock grows a paragraph per ticket. Today the steps are one frozen `LOOK_FIRST_STEPS`, and `lookFirstStep` builds its `why` from a slice of it. A one-line skip ("gate-marked → start at scoping") would leave the `why` saying the Surveys "have been attempted" when they never ran. The step list has to become per-ticket, and the `why` has to come from it.

**What the obvious way adds.** A sixth place that asks "is this a Periodical's review?" by parsing the marker inline. The others: `routes/proxy-writes.js:460` and `lib/periodical-report-gate.js:116` (`extractPeriodicalGateId`), `lib/dispatch-entrance.js:1582/1858` and `routes/proxy.js:1483/1557` (`resolvePeriodicalIdFromGateMarker`), and the prose rule in `lib/prompts/autopilot-precedence.js`. None uses a named predicate. Also, `MARKER_RE` matches anywhere in the description, not just the first line inside `## As asked`, so a ticket that quotes the marker skips both Surveys. The Done gate shares that breadth but fails loudly (it refuses Done). This would fail silently: two runs that just don't happen.

These would need to learn about it, and no test would catch a miss:
- `lib/proxy-instructions.js:920` ("code sends them first on a fresh ticket")
- `docs/architecture/prompt-system.md:7` (the look-first sentence and its restated invariant)
- `docs/architecture/source-map.md:217`
- `docs/plans/survey.md:96`
- the module docblock's "When it applies"

**Retired.** The two automatic Survey runs on gate-marked tickets, including survey-place's reading of the area-note edits that Stage-2 PRs land. Those tickets land a docs-only PR, so the rationale should say "no code", not "no change".

**Better, at this task's cost:**
- Add `isPeriodicalReview(description)` next to `extractPeriodicalGateId` in `lib/periodicals.js`, so the new caller names the question.
- Make a small pure `lookFirstSteps(description)`, with today's list as the default. The `why` and the tests read from it.
- Tests: a gate-marked case (selects `scoping`, no Survey claim in `why`), an unmarked twin (selects `survey-task`), and a `kind: survey-task` override that still pins.
- One clause per doc above, not a new paragraph.

**Better still, not this task's:**
- Move the other call sites onto the predicate.
- Decide whether the marker counts only inside `## As asked`. That changes the Done gate too, so it is one decision for every reader.
- Give the marker parser its own module. Today a route module imports the 1,386-line `lib/periodicals.js` registry for one regex.
- Gate-marked tickets that were never sealed already skip look-first and get past the Done gate. A separate gap.

## LIN-4398 implementation: PR ready, CI green

PR: https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2391 (branch `feat/lin-4398-periodical-review-skip-surveys`, commit b369ff3bb)

**What changed.** A gate-marked Periodical review now starts at `scoping`, with no `survey-task` or `survey-place` run. Every other ticket keeps both Surveys. Retired: the two automatic Survey runs on gate-marked Periodical reviews, including survey-place's reading of the area-note edits they land. Kept: scoping, manual `kind` overrides, and all Survey and scoping prompt text.

**Evidence.**
- New tests, red first against pre-change stubs (5 failed for the expected reasons), then green: `tests/unit/lin-4370-look-first-route.test.js` 52/52.
- Mutation checks, restored after each: route ignoring the predicate, old `why` slice, loose predicate, and override reading the route all fail their tests.
- Full unit run: 24,789 pass. The 2 remaining failures are not from this change: `scripts/code-shape/wrappers.test.mjs` fails identically on `main`.
- CI on the PR: Unit tests, E2E shards 1–4, secret scan, and CI success are all green.

**Not landed: the Waiting entry.** `docs/areas/llm-and-prompts.md` is at 6,139 of its 6,144-byte cap, so the area-notes guard rejects any addition. Filing it means pruning existing entries or changing the cap, which is a team decision. Content for the entry: the gate marker is read by more places than `isPeriodicalReview` (`routes/proxy-writes.js`, `lib/periodical-report-gate.js`, `lib/dispatch-entrance.js`, `routes/proxy.js`); it matches anywhere in a description, so a quoted marker skips both Surveys; deferred are reader consolidation, a parser module, the marker-location policy (with the Done gate), and unsealed marked tickets.

**Acceptance still open.** Merge is not mine. After merge, check that the next minted Periodical review's run list shows scoping and its work with no Survey run, and that the next ordinary fresh ticket shows both Surveys.

## Autopilot note: area-note Waiting entry (LIN-4398, PR #2391)

The implementation worker could not add the planned `## Waiting` entry to `docs/areas/llm-and-prompts.md`: the note is at 6139 of its 6144-byte cap. Engineering call, made by Autopilot: the PR goes to review **without** that entry. The deferred items it would have recorded (marker-reader consolidation, parser extraction, marker-location policy, unsealed-ticket gap) are already recorded on this ticket under Open questions and Changelog, so nothing is lost.

Not settled here, because they are John's calls (what to retire, guard policy): pruning other entries in that note, or raising `NOTE_BYTE_CAP`. The worker's open ruling `lin4398-area-note-cap` covers them; it does not hold this PR.

Also noted for the record: the implementation worker ran on `claude-haiku-5-5` and the plan worker on `sonnet`, not `opus` as the run asked.

## Review — LIN-4398

Reviewed [PR #2391](https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2391) at head `b369ff3bb7d19f9b83467677b1e6388b43d62240` (base `a36ad6195`; `origin/main` has moved by one commit since, LIN-4407's docs PR, which touches none of these files).

CI: green on b369ff3bb: Unit tests, E2E shards 1–4, secret scan, CI success.

**Scope matches the plan.** 7 files: `lib/periodicals.js` (+`isPeriodicalReview`), `lib/recommendation-look-first.js` (`lookFirstSteps` and a `why` built from the per-ticket list), one clause each in `lib/proxy-instructions.js`, `docs/architecture/prompt-system.md` (3 places), `docs/architecture/source-map.md` and `docs/plans/survey.md`, and tests. Nothing goes beyond the plan. The planned `## Waiting` entry is missing because the note is at 6,139/6,144 bytes. Autopilot waived it, and ruling `lin4398-area-note-cap` stays open. That is a leftover, not a defect.

**Checked myself, not taken from the builder's notes**
- **Real producer input.** I fed the actual `## As asked` blocks of the two live minted Periodical reviews, LIN-4406 (documentation-review) and LIN-4407 (integration-surface-maturity), through `lookFirstOff`/`lookFirstStep` at the PR head. Each has the marker as the first line inside the block, and both got both Surveys under today's code. With this PR both give `lookFirstOff = null` and step `scoping`. The reason reads "a Periodical review lands no code, so survey-task and survey-place are skipped; … so scoping is next". It does not claim "attempted". LIN-4398's own As-asked block (no marker) still gives `survey-task` with the old reason text.
- **Tests.** `tests/unit/lin-4370-look-first-route.test.js`: 52/52 locally.
- **Mutation checks**, each reverted afterwards (worktree clean):
  - M1: `lookFirstSteps` always returns `LOOK_FIRST_STEPS`. 4 red, including the recommend-and-dispatch seam test.
  - M2: `done` built from the old `LOOK_FIRST_STEPS.slice`. 1 red, the "no attempted claim" witness.
  - M3: `isPeriodicalReview` always true. 19 red, so the guard and twin tests hold.
  - M4: the skip lead removed from `why`. 1 red.
- **Every surface.** `codeRoutedRecommendation` (lib/openrouter.js:2073) is the only caller of `lookFirstStep`, and both seams use it (`openrouter.js:1123` buffered, `:2151` streamed). The Periodical autopilot kickoff reaches it through recommend-and-dispatch: that is how LIN-4406/4407 got their Surveys. There is no surface-specific bypass. The streamed seam has no marked-ticket test of its own, but it shares the one function, so I don't count that as a gap.
- **Constraints.** No new field or label, and no second parser: the new predicate wraps `extractPeriodicalGateId`. `LOOK_FIRST_STEPS` is still exported and unchanged. No Survey or scoping template changed, so no render changes, which honours `docs/areas/llm-and-prompts.md` LIN-4369 "keep scoping and both Survey renders byte-identical". No Periodical merge rule was added (LIN-4390 note). The `kind: survey-task` override still pins on a marked ticket (tested). The wording says "no code", never "no change".

**Regression check.** `git log -- <files>`: the recent commits are LIN-4392 (live-stage wait) and LIN-4390 (Periodical hand-off). The change leaves `lookFirstOff`, `holdingComment` and the live wait untouched, and the LIN-4392 tests in the same file stay green. Nothing reverted is re-applied.

**One of a class?** The behaviour lives in one place: no code outside `recommendation-look-first.js` lists the Surveys as a sequence. The other marker readers (`routes/proxy-writes.js`, `lib/periodical-report-gate.js`, `lib/dispatch-entrance.js`, `routes/proxy.js`) are a different class: identity for gating, not Survey routing. They fall **outside** this ticket's bounded class. Their consolidation is already deferred (plan, both Surveys, Open questions).

**Leftovers, one home each**
- **Fix on the PR branch (close-out does it).** `docs/plans/survey.md:96`, same sentence as the new clause: "so scoping always comes after both Surveys have ended" is now false for a marked review. Change it to "so scoping always comes after any Survey before it has ended".
- **Waiting entry for `lib/periodicals.js`** (marker readers, parser module, marker-location policy with the Done gate, unsealed marked tickets). Its home waits on ruling `lin4398-area-note-cap`. Close-out should not file it separately, or it would live in two places.

**Not a code finding, for the record.** Autopilot's note that implementation ran on `claude-haiku-5-5` rather than `opus`. The checks above are model-independent and I found no defect that traces to it.

### What CI Did Not Prove
- **Inside: "Done when", live behaviour (After the deploy).** The first Periodical review minted after deploy (Stage-1 mint with `<!-- harbour-periodical-gate id="…" -->` as the first line inside `## As asked`) shows `scoping` as its first stage run and no `survey-task`/`survey-place` run. The scoping recommendation's reason says "survey-task and survey-place are skipped". The next ordinary fresh ticket without the marker shows survey-task, then survey-place, then scoping. Check both tickets' run lists. This is a post-deploy step, not a merge condition.
- **Inside: producer emits the marker where the route reads it.** Discharged before the merge: the real LIN-4406 and LIN-4407 descriptions route to `scoping` at this head (probe above).
- **Rollback.** Revert the merge commit of PR #2391. It is pure routing with no persisted data or migration, so it is fully reversible.

### Verdict
Approve — conditional on close-out discharging the ledger

Against the As-asked block, sentence by sentence:
- "Every fresh task starts with two Surveys…", the context sentences, and John's two quotes are the rationale. The code keeps both Surveys for every unmarked ticket (twin and guard tests, and M3).
- "A Periodical's own review ticket changes no code, yet runs both today." I confirmed this on the live LIN-4406 and LIN-4407 Survey comments.
- "A Periodical's review ticket goes to its work without the Surveys." Met: a marked ticket goes straight to `scoping`, which leads to its work. Scoping is kept because the block names only the Surveys, and the plan records that.
- "Every other task keeps both." Met (guard, twin, mention tests).
- "Done when … runs without the Surveys, and other tasks still get both." Met in code and on real descriptions. The live run-list check is the ledger's post-deploy item.
- "Every change names what it retires." Met: the PR and module docblock name the two automatic Survey runs on marked reviews, including survey-place's reading of their area-note edits.
- "Questions…": the engineering questions (scoping kept, marker matched anywhere) were settled by the work. The one John call (note cap) is a ruling and does not hold the PR.

Next: close-out makes the `docs/plans/survey.md` fix above, re-checks CI on that commit, merges, and records the post-deploy check.

## Close-out — LIN-4398

**What merged.** [PR #2391](https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2391) as merge commit `008d38bb088ca824f433940a227bffc27f3a60a1`, pinned with `--match-head-commit 821ef78a0e84e8c4d62ba71d42107f530f35b295`. A gate-marked Periodical review now starts at `scoping` with no `survey-task` or `survey-place` run; every other ticket keeps both Surveys. Review's account (the Approve comment, sentence by sentence against the As-asked block) is how it meets the ask. Retired: the two automatic Survey runs on gate-marked reviews, including survey-place's reading of their area-note edits.

**Changes I made after the approval (one).**
- `821ef78a0` — `docs/plans/survey.md:96`: "so scoping always comes after both Surveys have ended" → "so scoping always comes after any Survey before it has ended". Answers review's "Fix on the PR branch" leftover. No code or assertion changed.

**CI.** CI exists (`.github/workflows/test.yml`). Re-established on the new head `821ef78a0`: Unit tests, E2E shards 1–4, Secret scan, CI success all green; merged pinned to that commit. `origin/main` had moved (LIN-4405, LIN-4407); GitHub reported the PR mergeable and the merge was conflict-free.

**Ledger.**
- *Inside — live behaviour after deploy.* Deploy landed (harbour.cat footer moved from `d948009` to a commit containing `008d38bb`). Checked on what landed, via `GET /issues/{id}/recommend` (read-only, nothing dispatched):
  - **LIN-4398 → LIN-4411**, a Security Review Periodical minted after the merge, with `<!-- harbour-periodical-gate id="security-review" -->` as the first line inside `## As asked`: `recommendedAction: scoping`, reason "a Periodical review lands no code, so survey-task and survey-place are skipped; no size of the move is recorded, so scoping is next". It has 0 dispatches so far, so no `survey-task`/`survey-place` run exists on it.
  - **LIN-4410**, an ordinary sealed, unmarked ticket with no runs: `recommendedAction: survey-task`, reason with no skip claim. The survey-task → survey-place → scoping order beyond the first step is covered by the PR's route tests (52/52); I did not dispatch LIN-4410, so its later steps have not been observed live. Both seams share this one function (review).
  - Still to observe, with no action needed from me: LIN-4411's run list once it is dispatched should show `scoping` first and no Survey runs.
- *Inside — producer emits marker where the route reads it.* Discharged before merge by review (LIN-4406/LIN-4407 real descriptions), and now again on LIN-4411.
- *Rollback.* Review's named rollback: revert merge commit `008d38bb`. Pure routing, no persisted data or migration.
- *Outside / Waiting entry.* Not filed here: review put its home behind open ruling `lin4398-area-note-cap` (John's call on pruning `docs/areas/llm-and-prompts.md` or raising `NOTE_BYTE_CAP`, 6,139/6,144 bytes), so filing a ticket too would put it in two places. Deferred items (marker-reader consolidation, parser module, marker-location policy with the Done gate, unsealed marked tickets) stay recorded on this ticket and in that ruling. No new follow-up tickets filed; no related tickets to close (no relations on this ticket).

**Worker model note** (from Autopilot): implementation ran on `claude-haiku-5-5`, plan on `sonnet`, not `opus`; review found no defect from it.

**Description.** Pre-prune snapshot archived (latest of 7 snapshots equals the pre-prune description, verified); the discharged plan below the block is pruned to a stub.
